decisions.question: Jira v1 — client shape: REST-only gateway endpoints mirroring `/api/v1/gh/*`, or bundle a Jira CLI (`jira-cli` / `go-jira`) in the sandbox?

options.label: Option A: REST-only gateway endpoints (recommended — mirrors gh wrapper, no binary to secure)
Option B: Bundle a Jira CLI in the sandbox
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: REST-only gateway endpoints (recommended — mirrors gh wrapper, no binary to secure)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — auth flavor: Atlassian Cloud API token (email + token, Basic), OAuth 2.0 3LO, or pluggable from day one?

options.label: Option A: API token / Basic auth (recommended — matches existing secrets.template.env, bot identity, headless bootstrap)
Option B: OAuth 2.0 3LO (granular scopes, rotating refresh tokens, but user-attributed and consent flow)
Option C: Pluggable from day one (both strategies)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: API token / Basic auth (recommended — matches existing secrets.template.env, bot identity, headless bootstrap)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — how should "private network mode only" be enforced at the route layer?

options.label: Option A: Per-route check of g.session_mode + a @require_private_mode decorator (recommended — consistent with existing gh endpoints)
Option B: Flask blueprint with a before_request reject (introduces blueprint usage only for Jira)
Option C: Extend @require_session_auth with a required_mode="private" kwarg (touches a widely-used decorator)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: Per-route check of g.session_mode + a @require_private_mode decorator (recommended — consistent with existing gh endpoints)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — endpoint surface: narrow verbs + regex-filtered `execute` passthrough, one big `execute` only, or narrow verbs only with no passthrough?

options.label: Option A: Three narrow verbs (ticket/get, search, ticket/comments) + regex-filtered /api/v1/jira/execute passthrough (recommended)
Option B: Single /api/v1/jira/execute passthrough only
Option C: Three narrow verbs only; no execute passthrough
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: Three narrow verbs (ticket/get, search, ticket/comments) + regex-filtered /api/v1/jira/execute passthrough (recommended)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — where should the project allowlist live?

options.label: Option A: New jira: section in config/context-filters.yaml (recommended — reuses a file operators already edit)
Option B: New dedicated config/jira.yaml
Option C: Env var JIRA_PROJECT_ALLOWLIST on the gateway
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: New jira: section in config/context-filters.yaml (recommended — reuses a file operators already edit)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — search implementation: use Atlassian's `/rest/api/3/search/jql` directly, or build our own index over synced ticket data?

options.label: Option A: Use /rest/api/3/search/jql (recommended — the only non-deprecated search verb on Jira Cloud)
Option B: Ship our own index over synced ticket data (much bigger scope; avoids Atlassian API quirks)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: Use /rest/api/3/search/jql (recommended — the only non-deprecated search verb on Jira Cloud)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — identity: should the gateway authenticate as a dedicated Atlassian bot account, or reuse the operator's personal Atlassian account?

options.label: Option A: Dedicated bot account (recommended — clean audit attribution, low-privilege role)
Option B: Operator's personal Atlassian account (simpler bootstrap, uglier audit)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Gateway accepts an API token via secrets.env, same pattern as GitHub. The token can be either a bot account or a user account — don't constrain identity in the gateway code; that's an operator choice."}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — response redaction: should the gateway strip `accountId`, `emailAddress`, and attachment URLs from responses before returning them to the sandbox?

options.label: Option A: Redact accountId, emailAddress, and attachment URLs (recommended — reduces incidental PII leakage to sandbox)
Option B: Pass responses through verbatim
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "No redaction needed. Jira endpoints are private-mode only — sessions in private mode are a constrained, trusted context, so passing accountId/emailAddress/attachment URLs through verbatim is acceptable."}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — EGG_JIRA_TICKET scoping: is it advisory context (agent can hit any ticket in allowlisted projects) or an enforcement boundary (agent can only hit that specific ticket + its comments)?

options.label: Option A: Advisory only; project allowlist is the only hard boundary (recommended — search and cross-ticket reads work naturally)
Option B: Enforced; agents can only access the one ticket named by EGG_JIRA_TICKET and its comments
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: Advisory only; project allowlist is the only hard boundary (recommended — search and cross-ticket reads work naturally)"}

decisions.question: Jira v1 — multi-tenancy: should v1 assume a single Atlassian site (and leave the second-site seam open for a follow-up), or support multiple sites from day one?

options.label: Option A: Single site in v1; keep the client architecture ready for multi-site (recommended)
Option B: Multi-site from day one (multiple JIRA_BASE_URL entries, key-scoped routing)
Other (explain in reply)

decisions.resolution: {"action": "select", "selected": "Option A: Single site in v1; keep the client architecture ready for multi-site (recommended)"}

For the `/api/v1/jira/execute` passthrough, is there any path pattern outside `GET /rest/api/3/issue/...`, `GET /rest/api/3/search/...`, and `GET /rest/api/3/project/...` you want permitted in v1?
How should the gateway handle deleted / archived tickets in responses — 404 passthrough, or synthesize a `{"status":"not_found"}` envelope for consistency with other gateway endpoints?

Looking ahead to the future write scope (create ticket / update ticket / create comment, out of scope here but informing v1 design): should the gateway enforce idempotency (e.g., refuse duplicate `comment create` within N seconds), or leave that to Atlassian's own semantics?

Is the intent strictly "private mode only" for Jira, or do you anticipate a hypothetical "internal-dev" mode (trusted agents, locked-down network) that should also see Jira endpoints? (No such mode exists today.)
Which Atlassian projects should be on the v1 allowlist? (Provide project keys, comma-separated, e.g. `ENG,WEBAPP,INFRA`.)
questions.answer: Configurable — project allowlist lives in the new `jira:` section of `config/context-filters.yaml`; ops populate it at setup time. Gateway ships with an empty allowlist (fails closed on any project).

questions.question: What is the expected request volume per pipeline (peak JQL searches/min, peak ticket reads/min)? This feeds rate-limit defaults.
questions.answer: Low (<10/min each) for v1. Rate-limit defaults should be conservative and tunable via gateway config.

questions.question: Is there a preferred Atlassian bot-account naming / identity convention (display name, email, avatar) we should align with, or is this greenfield?
questions.answer: Greenfield — pick at setup; no existing convention to align with.

questions.question: Beyond `accountId`, `emailAddress`, and attachment URLs, are there custom fields or other response fields we should redact before sandbox-visible responses?
questions.answer: N/A — no redaction. Jira is private-mode only, and in that mode the session is already a constrained, trusted context (matches earlier decision on redaction).

questions.question: On Atlassian 429 (rate-limited) responses with `Retry-After`: pass the 429 through verbatim to the sandbox, or have the gateway swallow + retry once with honoured backoff?
questions.answer: Gateway swallows + retries once, honouring `Retry-After`. If the retry also fails, pass the 429 through so the failure still surfaces to the agent.

questions.question: Should Jira audit logs ship to the same sink as existing gateway audit logs, or a separate Jira-scoped sink?
questions.answer: Same sink as existing gateway audit logs. Jira ops are tagged in structured log entries so they can be filtered at query time.

questions.question: For the `/api/v1/jira/execute` passthrough, is there any path pattern outside `GET /rest/api/3/issue/...`, `GET /rest/api/3/search/...`, and `GET /rest/api/3/project/...` you want permitted in v1?
questions.answer: No — only `GET /rest/api/3/issue/...`, `GET /rest/api/3/search/...`, and `GET /rest/api/3/project/...`. Anything outside those three families requires a narrow route (future work).

questions.question: How should the gateway handle deleted / archived tickets in responses — 404 passthrough, or synthesize a `{"status":"not_found"}` envelope for consistency with other gateway endpoints?
questions.answer: Synthesize `{"status":"not_found"}` envelope — consistent with how other gateway endpoints shape errors.

questions.question: Looking ahead to the future write scope (create ticket / update ticket / create comment, out of scope here but informing v1 design): should the gateway enforce idempotency (e.g., refuse duplicate `comment create` within N seconds), or leave that to Atlassian's own semantics?
questions.answer: Out of scope for v1 (which is read-only). When writes land, start by relying on Atlassian's own semantics + operator discipline rather than gateway-enforced idempotency; revisit only if duplicate-write issues surface.

questions.question: Is the intent strictly "private mode only" for Jira, or do you anticipate a hypothetical "internal-dev" mode (trusted agents, locked-down network) that should also see Jira endpoints? (No such mode exists today.)
questions.answer: Private mode only. No internal-dev mode exists today, and inventing one just to widen Jira reachability is out of scope for #1556. If such a mode is added later, reachability for Jira can be reconsidered then.
